column1: *** THE CORDON'S DEATH REGISTERS, WORKED AT LAST ***
column2: full text, surname against the Cordon parish, filtered to its DEATH and BURIAL volumes - 13 October 2026
column3: *** THIRTEEN DOCUMENTS, AND THE SEAM IS FINALLY A SIZE A PERSON CAN READ ***
column4: The parish was sized on 12 October at about 95 documents across 43 volumes; the four adults of Sarandi 229 were the reason for coming.
column5: *** Thirteen of the ninety-five sit in the Cordon's own death and burial books *** - Religious Death Records 1839-1852, 1869-1877; Religious Burial Records 1885-1892, 1892-1897, 1897-1901, 1908-1914 and 1918-1926. *** That is the list, and it is the first time this archive has had one. *** Two were read today; eleven are unread.

column1: *** AND THE FIRST ONE OPENED CARRIES A DEATH NOBODY HERE KNEW ***
column2: Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Religious Death Records June 1869 - February 1877; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BSFN-Z, *** PLATE READ *** at apid TH-909-52378-67990-19
column3: *** TWO SISTERS, AGED FOUR AND THREE, DIED ON THE SAME DAY ***
column4: Nothing. Neither child nor their parents were in this register.
column5: *** 'En cinco de Agosto de mil ochoc.s sesenta y nueve, MURIERON Vicenta Lavina, de cuatro anos, y Manuela Lavina, de tres anos, hija de D. Xavier (hijo) y de LA FINADA LEONARDA LERENA.' *** Two deaths in one entry, five days into August 1869. *** And the mother was already dead when they died. ***

column1: *** WHICH WOULD MAKE IT A DEATH FOR A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE FOUND ON 12 OCTOBER ***
column2: the same act, against the padron of 1850 read on 12 October
column3: *** LEONARDA LERENA WAS DEAD BEFORE 5 AUGUST 1869 ***
column4: *** LEONARDA MARGARITA LERENA VEGA, born 20 February 1837 ***, was located on 12 October at casa 229 of Calle Sarandi in the padron of 1850 - entered at eleven, the only white person in a house of four adults who carried the surname by ditto.
column5: *** The fit is good and it is NOT a merge. *** The forename is uncommon; the parish is the one she was living in; her daughters were born about 1865 and 1866, when she would have been twenty-eight; and she is dead by 1869, at about thirty-two. *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: her own death act, or the girls' baptisms, which would name her parents. *** Neither is found - 'Leonarda Lerena' as a phrase returns ONE document in the whole corpus, and it is this one.

column1: *** AND THE FAMILY SHE MARRIED INTO IS NAMED ***
column2: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1857-1860, dispensation *** No. 395 of 1861 *** - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-VWDN-4, transcript read
column3: *** DON XAVIER LAVINA THE ELDER AND DONA MANUELA GOYENECHE ***
column4: The 1869 death act calls the father 'D. Xavier (hijo)' - the younger - which implies an elder of the same name and says nothing else about him.
column5: *** The dispensation is for a DIFFERENT son: 'Don EMILIO LAVINA Y GOYENECHE, de estado soltero, de edad de veinte y cuatro anos, natural de San Pedro del Durazno ... hijo legitimo de Don XAVIER LAVINA y Dona MANUELA GOYENECHE', marrying Dona Maria Eladia Ramona Mendoza. *** So Leonarda married into a family of Durazno origin, and her husband had a brother. *** A third Lavina record, in the Cordon marriage register of 1866-1872, is Xavier Lavina standing WITNESS at a stranger's wedding in January 1868 - not his own. ***

column1: *** AND THE TENTH DISPENSATION STILL DOES NOT EXIST ***
column2: the same dispensation, which surfaced by a route the 12 October sweep did not use
column3: *** TESTED AND IT HELD ***
column4: On 12 October this archive swept the Montevideo dispensation register on eight compound Lerena forms and concluded there is no tenth Lerena dispensation.
column5: *** This one arrived through a surname that is not Lerena at all - LAVINA - and so would have been invisible to that sweep. *** It is *** not *** a Lerena dispensation: the groom is a Lavina y Goyeneche and the bride a Mendoza. *** So the conclusion survives a test it was not designed for, which is worth more than the conclusion was. *** It also shows the shape of the next doubt: a Lerena BRIDE whose dispensation is filed under her husband's surname would be missed by every sweep run so far.

column1: *** AND ONE MORE DEATH, NOW AT THE PLATE ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Death Records 1869-1877, entry 619, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BS82-4 - *** PLATE READ *** 17 October 2026
column3: *** AMELIA LERENA, NINE YEARS OLD, DIED 11 NOVEMBER 1871 ***
column4: Nothing; she is new to this register.
column5: *** 'En once de Nov.e de 1871 murio Amelia Lerena, oriental, de nueve anos. Conste.' *** Born about 1862. *** NO PARENTS ARE NAMED. *** The machine transcript had run her margin into the next entry and set 'Giombalta' beside her; that is the entry below, Juan Giombatta de Tomassi. She is not merged with any Amelia in this register.

column1: *** WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND ***
column2: the four adults of casa 229 of Calle Sarandi
column3: *** STILL UNFOUND, AND THE FORENAME ROUTE IS TOO WIDE ***
column4: Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela and Rosa carry the surname by ditto in 1850; the holder formula was swept on 12 October and does not reach them.
column5: *** 'Estanislada' alone, with a Cordon place filter, returns NINE PAGES *** - about nine hundred documents - so the forename is not a handle either, and the compound forms return nothing. *** ALL THIRTEEN DEATH AND BURIAL PAGES THAT FULL TEXT RETURNS ARE NOW OPENED (17 October 2026) AND NONE OF THE FOUR IS IN THEM. *** That is a limit on the instrument, not a null on the books: each of the thirteen is the one PAGE where full text saw the surname, not the volume it sits in, and a name written without LERENA, or spelled so the machine missed it, is not on that list.

column1: *** ELEVEN MORE PAGES OPENED ON 17 OCTOBER, AND THE FOUR ARE STILL NOT IN THEM ***
column2: full text, the parish's DEATH and BURIAL volumes - the other eleven of the thirteen pages, each opened in the signed-in viewer, with the plate read for six
column3: *** ELEVEN LERENA ACTS, ONE ON EACH PAGE, AND SEVEN OF THE PEOPLE ARE NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE ***
column4: Two of the thirteen had been read; the rest were a list.
column5: *** The plate was read for the acts below that say so; the others are the machine transcript and are labelled. *** Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela of Africa and Rosa are in none of them. What the pages held instead is below: a man buried under his father's surname, a woman of eighteen born out of wedlock, a married couple and a widow, and the death of a husband who had been dead twenty-seven years when this archive thought him alive.

column1: *** A YOUNG MAN BURIED AS A LARRANAGA, WHOSE MOTHER WAS A LERENA ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SWL-D - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** JOSE MARIA LARRANAGA, TWENTY-TWO, BURIED 2 AUGUST 1890 ***
column4: Nothing. The Lerena is his mother's, so no search on the surname would have reached him.
column5: *** 'En dos de Agosto del ano mil ochocientos noventa se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Jose Maria Larranaga, oriental, soltero, de veintidos anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena. Fallecio ayer.' *** Three people are new: him, his father Benito and his mother MARTINA LERENA. Nothing places her in a Lerena family here, and nothing is merged.

column1: *** A MARRIED COUPLE FROM SAN JOSE MAY HAVE BEEN IN THE CORDON ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SW7-N - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** SERVANDO TOMAS GONZALEZ, 'CASADO CON ESTEFANA LERENA', BURIED 25 MAY 1892 ***
column4: The register holds a Servando Gonzalez and an Estefania Lerena at San Jose de Mayo, with six children indexed GONZALEZ LERENA, found on 11 October.
column5: *** 'En veinte y cinco de Mayo de mil ochocientos noventa y dos se manda dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Servando Tomas Gonzalez, oriental, casado con Estefana Lerena, ... cinco anos, de que certifico.' *** The transcript gives sixty-five. *** THIS IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A MERGE: *** the act gives no birthplace and no child, and San Jose to Montevideo is a move of department.

column1: *** A WOMAN OF EIGHTEEN, BORN OUT OF WEDLOCK, NAMED FOR HER MOTHER ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, image 252 of 255, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4S93-D - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** SARA LERENA, 'HIJA NATURAL DE TERESA LERENA', BURIED 18 AUGUST 1892 ***
column4: Nothing; she and her mother are new.
column5: *** 'En diez y ocho de Agosto de mil ochocientos noventa y dos se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Sara Lerena, soltera, hija natural de Teresa Lerena, orientales, que fallecio hoy de diez y ocho anos de edad.' *** *** HER SURNAME IS HER MOTHER'S, because 'natural' means no father is entered. *** Born about 1874. Neither is placed in a Lerena family here.

column1: *** THE 1896 DEATH OF PEDRO A. LERENA IS ALSO IN THE BURIAL BOOK ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records August 1892 - May 1897, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49R4-Y - machine transcript only
column3: *** BURIED 8 NOVEMBER 1896, AGED SIXTY-NINE, 'CASADO CON MANUELA LEMOS' ***
column4: His civil death registration of 7 November 1896 (acta 353) was read at the plate on 12 October.
column5: *** It agrees with the civil act on name, age and wife and adds nothing. *** The burial says 'fallecio ayer' on the 8th; the civil act says he died on the 6th, so the word is not a date.

column1: *** AN UNKNOWN LERENA WIDOW OF ABOUT SIXTY, AND THE QUESTION OF TERESA LEONARD ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records May 1897 - November 1901, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49TQ-6 - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** 'TERESA LEONOR DE LERENA', WIDOW, BURIED 27 AUGUST 1901 ***
column4: The register holds a Teresa Leonard, wife of Pedro Antonio Lerena and mother of Manuel Lerena Leonard, with no record of her own.
column5: *** 'Se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Teresa Leonor de Lerena, oriental, de sesenta [y ...] anos, viuda de [forename left blank] Lerena. Fallecio hoy.' *** It fits, and the plate says LEONOR, a given name, where the other woman's surname is LEONARD. *** A CANDIDATE AND NOT A MERGE. ***

column1: *** JULIA JUANICO'S BURIAL GIVES HER AGE FIVE YEARS WRONG ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records April 1908 - May 1914, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49PS-Q - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** BURIED 12 JULY 1910 AS 'JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA ... DE SESENTA Y DOS', WIDOW OF LUIS LERENA LENGUAS ***
column4: Her death of 11 July 1910 was read at the plate on 12 October, and her baptism of 1842 on 21 September.
column5: *** The day and the widowhood agree. The age does not: her baptism makes her sixty-seven. *** A burial entry's age is the priest's, not a second birth year. Her son Enrique's burial of 17 May 1914, aged forty-one, is on a second page of the same book and agrees with his civil act.

column1: *** MANUELA LEMOS'S BURIAL NAMES THE WRONG HUSBAND ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4S3R-S - machine transcript only
column3: *** BURIED 24 JULY 1918, AGED SEVENTY-SEVEN, 'VIUDA DE CARLOS LERENA' ***
column4: Her husband is Pedro A. Lerena, dead in 1896; Carlos Teodoro is one of her sons.
column5: *** She died about 23 July 1918, born about 1841. *** The entry gives her husband as Carlos, not Pedro; the 1896 civil act is the stronger source and the discrepancy is left standing.

column1: *** A HUSBAND WHO HAD BEEN DEAD TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SHT-C - plate read for the date
column3: *** CARLOS ALBERTO FEIN, SEVENTY-FIVE, 'CASADO CON ADELINA LERENA', BURIED 18 MAY 1919 ***
column4: He was entered only as the husband named on his wife's death registration of 20 November 1946, and a date-reading tool took that as placing him alive in 1946.
column5: *** He died about 17 May 1919, born about 1844. *** The 1946 registration names him as her husband without saying he was dead; it is not evidence that he was alive.

column1: *** A SECOND LERENA WOMAN MARRIED TO A MAN OF SEVENTY-SEVEN ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49BP-V - machine transcript only
column3: *** JOSE MARIA REYES, 'CASADO CON MARIA LERENA', BURIED 13 JUNE 1920 ***
column4: Nothing; both are new.
column5: *** 'Se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Jose Maria Reyes, oriental, de setenta y siete anos, casado con Maria Lerena; fallecio ayer.' *** The transcript has not been checked at the plate. No tie is claimed to the Maria Lerena of the 1908 enrolment card.

column1: *** THE EARLIEST BOOK GIVES NOTHING THAT WAS NOT ALREADY HELD ***
column2: Cordon, Religious Death Records October 1839 - January 1852, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BSXL-R - machine transcript
column3: *** CARMEN LERENA, THREE, BURIED 14 AUGUST 1841 ***
column4: Her act was read at the plate on 20 September 2026 off the cemetery's own register, and her father Justo Lerena and mother Juana Quintana are already rows.
column5: *** This is the same act on a second film, with the same priest. *** The page opened has the Names panel read 'Carmen Lerena Lerena', which is the machine doubling the surname that the earlier plate reading already rejected.

column1: *** THE LARRANAGA FAMILY IS A FAMILY NOW, AND THE MOTHER IS A LERENA OF ABOUT 1846 ***
column2: Montevideo, Death Records 1884-1886, the civil act of 29 March 1885, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-Z9LY-F - *** PLATE READ *** - found by an exact-phrase full-text search on 'Martina Lerena', four results
column3: *** BENITO LARRANAGA, SPANISH, SEVENTY, DIED 28 MARCH 1885, 'CASADO CON DONA MARTINA LERENA, ORIENTAL, DE TREINTA Y NUEVE ANOS' ***
column4: Both were named only, on the Cordon burial of their son in August 1890.
column5: *** Seven children are named: Benito, Carmen, Jose Maria, Ygnacio, Donato, Doroteo and Antonia. *** He died at 3 a.m. in calle Defensa 22, five years before the son's burial. Martina is born about 1846 and is a Lerena by birth - and her own baptism is NOT in the record index for 1840-1852 and no act gives her parents, so she is still unplaced. Six siblings are new rows, named only.

column1: *** AND THE SON'S OWN CIVIL ACT GIVES HIM A TRADE AND A DEATH ***
column2: Montevideo civil death registration no. 121 of 2 August 1890, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-K3NM-S - *** PLATE READ *** (no machine transcript exists for this image)
column3: *** JOSE MARIA LARRANAGA, A COACHMAN OF TWENTY-TWO, DIED OF CONSUMPTION ON 1 AUGUST 1890 ***
column4: His burial at the Cordon, read earlier the same day.
column5: *** 'ha fallecido Jose Maria Larranaga ... de veintidos anos ... de estado soltero y de profesion cochero, a consecuencia de tisis pulmonar, segun consta del certificado del Dr. Lisazo' *** at 18 de Julio 847, ten-thirty in the morning, 'hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena'. The burial and the civil act agree on name, age and parents.

column1: *** THE SAN JOSE CANDIDATE, TESTED AGAINST THE INDEX ***
column2: FamilySearch record index, surname Gonzalez Lerena with the father's forename Servando, Uruguay - 17 October 2026, *** INDEX ONLY ***
column3: *** THE CANDIDATE SURVIVES, AND TWO OF THE SONS DIED AT MONTEVIDEO ***
column4: The 1892 burial was a candidate for the San Jose couple Servando Gonzalez and Estefania Lerena, with nothing to test it.
column5: *** Children born 1854, about 1856, 1858 (Corina, now read at the plate) and 1872, all before May 1892. *** Servando Cecilio died at Montevideo on 11 October 1911 and Leopoldo, father of Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena, on 17 June 1922. A Servando of about sixty-five in 1892 fits. *** STILL NOT MERGED: *** no act names the couple at Montevideo, and some 1930-32 index cards give the same parents for women who would then be fifty or more at marriage. Three people are new rows, index-level.

column1: *** THE SAN JOSE COUPLE WERE AT TRINIDAD, FLORES, IN 1858 AND 1884 ***
column2: Santisima Trinidad marriage of 20 February 1884, index ark 1:1:XS6J-DWBY - *** INDEX ONLY ***
column3: *** ESPERANZA GONZALEZ, 26, MARRIED DAMASO NEGROTTO; HER PARENTS ARE SERVANDO SANTA MARINA GONZALEZ AND ESTEFANIA LERENA ***
column4: Corina Francisca's christening at Trinidad in 1858 had 'Nefania' and Servando Gonzalez as parents, unattached.
column5: *** The family lived at Trinidad from 1858 to 1884, and two sons later died at Montevideo. *** It does not test the 1892 burial any further, because it says nothing of where Servando was in 1892. A computer-indexed record; a family-tree user has attached it to a 'Estefania Lerena Fernandez, born 1832', which is unsourced and not used.

column1: *** THE 1858 BAPTISM NAMES HER, AND THE INDEX HAD LOST HER SURNAME ***
column2: Santisima Trinidad, Baptism Records October 1857 - August 1866, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HW-7 - *** PLATE READ ***
column3: *** CORINA FRANCISCA GONZALEZ, BORN 24 JULY 1858, 'HIJA LEGITIMA DE SERVANDO GONZALEZ Y DE ESTEFANIA LERENA, ORIENTALES' ***
column4: The index gave her mother only as 'Nefania' and she was a probable child of the couple.
column5: *** She is confirmed as theirs, and the surname Lerena is in the act itself. *** It adds no parent for Estefania, and it does not test the 1892 burial; it fixes the household at Trinidad in 1858.
